red_team_findings: The dominant Week 3 issue was decision-layer override, not failure of the final pre-lock model snapshot: all eight entry wagers placed opposite the model lost.
The four A/A- model sides all covered, but this is a one-week sample and should not cause confidence inflation or stake escalation by itself.

Earlier external/context convergence on CAR -2.5 and the earlier SEA -7.5 view conflicted with the final pre-lock V2 layer; the system needs a hard final-decision reconciliation step so stale earlier views cannot silently override the latest authoritative model state.
SportsLine exact ATS and Gridiron exact-line directional takes were each 4-4; Lucas was 2-5. Week 3 does not justify mathematically weighting these sources into V2 probabilities.
Stake sizing remains a separate concern. The result supports improving final signal reconciliation before changing the optimizer's risk objective or increasing deployment.

BUF line provenance requires cleanup: the pre-lock model layer stored BUF -7 while the user's final wager screenshot records BUF -6. The result covered both, so settlement is unaffected, but the frozen Sly-line source of truth must be singular going forward.
week4_actions: Make the final pre-lock model snapshot the explicit decision baseline, with any override requiring a recorded reason and source timestamp.
Add an automatic model-vs-submitted-side reconciliation check before wagers are finalized.
Continue prospective shadow scoring without retraining from Week 3 alone.
Keep external sources contextual until sufficient prospective evidence supports weighting them.
Resolve frozen-line provenance before Week 4 recommendations, especially when a submitted line differs from the canonical model snapshot.
